versions.changelog: Simplify the login instructions to the code flow (maton login prints a link; finish with maton login --code <CODE>), drop the API Key subsection, and pin the Maton CLI install to 0.4.0.
Switch the login instructions to the device flow (maton login prints a link and a user code; the --oauth flag is gone) and pin the Maton CLI install to 0.3.5.
Pin the Maton CLI install to 0.3.4, the current release.

Add this skill's own trigger policy to the shared Triggers section: the only destination it sets up is its own hosted function inside the platform, it does not forward events to third-party hosts, and it does not use event watch --exec; each trigger reference now also says this skill configures no trigger from that source on its own.

Bring the skill to the current api-gateway baseline and tell the connection-to-function-to-trigger story: the shared Functions and Triggers sections open with an example for this app (a hosted function that performs one action for it through the Maton SDK, and the trigger that runs it - its own event source where it has one, otherwise a time schedule), the description says these constructs turn the connection into automation and add no capability of their own, the passthrough is described by its enforced boundary, CLI and SDK installs are pinned to 0.3.1, absolute API URLs are placeholders, and multipart uploads use mktemp.

Resolve remaining audit findings: state one consistent endpoint policy instead of conflicting scope claims, qualify the local-execution and high-impact wording, note that locale examples are illustrative, and correct app-specific auth, method and upload-path documentation

Address security-audit findings: disclose the api passthrough in the access-scope and description text, warn on irreversible connection deletion, add response data-minimization guidance, and correct app-specific auth and request-body notes
CLI-first rewrite with the Maton SDK examples; clarify that the CLI and SDKs keep separate credential stores, and reword webhook egress warnings

CLI-first rewrite: the maton CLI with OAuth login is the documented path, every example is a maton command, SDK examples added, and the raw HTTP fallback feeds the key on stdin instead of reading it from the environment

- Expanded scope from read-only to full admin access, including write, delete, and member file access capabilities.
- Updated description and documentation to clarify that all write/delete and member-file-access operations require explicit user approval with resource identifiers and business justification.
- Emphasized the privacy sensitivity of member file access and advised caution.
- Cleaned up documentation to clarify Maton platform connection endpoints versus Dropbox API endpoints.
- Removed the sample skill-card.md file.

- Clarified that the skill defaults to read-only access; write operations now require explicit user approval with specific resource details.
- Enhanced security and permissions section: instructs users to always confirm resource identities and intended effects before write actions.
- Added caution guidance for high-impact actions (e.g., member removals, folder deletions).
- Refined description and usage guidance to emphasize viewing/listing data and explicit user confirmation for changes.
- API usage instructions now specify to use only the documented endpoints.

- Updated API and connection base URLs from gateway.maton.ai and ctrl.maton.ai to api.maton.ai.
- Clarified security and permissions section; emphasized explicit user confirmation for write operations.
- Modified connection management instructions to reflect new endpoint URLs.
- Added note to always include the `Maton-Connection` header if using multiple connections.
- Removed LICENSE.txt file from the repository.

- Expanded API reference with advanced features, including team feature queries and authenticated admin info.
- Added documentation for v2 endpoints (e.g., members/list_v2, members/get_info_v2) for richer member and role data.
- Included more sample responses and parameter examples for clarity.
- No changes to code or implementation; documentation improvements only.

No user-facing changes in this release.  
- Version bump to 1.0.2 with no file changes detected.

- Added metadata fields specifying required environment variable (MATON_API_KEY), homepage URL, and emoji for skill identification.
- No changes to functionality or usage instructions.

Initial release of Dropbox Business skill with managed OAuth and team administration capabilities.

- Provides secure Dropbox Business API access with managed OAuth authentication via Maton.
- Enables management of team members, groups, folders, devices, apps, and audit logs.
- Supports team/team member operations: list, add, suspend, unsuspend, remove, and get info.
- Includes sample code for API usage and connection management.
- Requires network access and a valid Maton API key.
